jobs.title: Sr. Director Analytics Automation, Audit & Advisory Services
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Senior Director, Automation is a key member of the Data Analytics team, responsible for leading the delivery of automation and AI solutions, as well as analytics supporting audit engagements, across Audit & Advisory Services globally. The role combines innovation, critical thinking, technical expertise, and strong business acumen to translate audit and business needs into practical, scalable, secure, production-ready solutions that measurably enhance audit efficiency, coverage, and assurance.

You will provide leadership across solution design, development and implementation, audit analytics delivery, project execution, stakeholder management, adoption, and data and AI governance, leveraging data, analytics, automation, and AI to advance the Audit & Advisory Services strategy. This position reports to the AVP, Data Analytics, Audit & Advisory Services.

Position Responsibilities

Automation Portfolio Leadership & Delivery:

Oversee the portfolio of automation projects across the team, providing end-to-end leadership from solution design and planning through development, implementation, and hand-off.
Provide technical and functional expertise in the design of automation and analytics solutions, challenging proposed approaches and guiding the team toward practical, scalable, and sustainable solutions.
Establish project plans, estimate effort and timelines, define milestones and resource requirements, and monitor execution against agreed deliverables.
Proactively identify delivery risks, dependencies, and technical or business challenges; work with the team and stakeholders to resolve roadblocks and adjust delivery plans as required.
Maintain accountability for project execution, ensuring solutions are delivered on time, within scope, and to expected quality standards.

Portfolio Governance & Senior Management Reporting

Provide regular, transparent reporting to senior management on project status, milestones, risks, dependencies, resource requirements, and expected completion dates.
Assess project progress and viability and provide clear recommendations on the appropriate course of action, including whether to persist, pause, reprioritize, redesign, or stop an initiative.
Own and continuously improve the team's delivery framework, including intake, business requirements, solution design, stage gates, and monthly portfolio reviews.

Stakeholder Management

Build strong relationships with Audit leaders, project sponsors, audit teams, enterprise technology, data, and risk partners, and other stakeholders throughout solution development and implementation.
Establish and actively manage stakeholder expectations regarding scope, functionality, timelines, dependencies, risks, and resource requirements.
Facilitate alignment when stakeholder expectations and technical or delivery realities differ, recommending pragmatic options and providing clear escalation when necessary.
effort, time savings and other benefits for every solution released to production.

AI Risk & Governance

Audit Analytics Delivery

Provide oversight and technical guidance throughout analytics engagements to ensure solutions appropriately address the audit objective and can be executed within agreed timelines.

People Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop team members responsible for automation and analytics delivery, providing regular feedback, technical guidance, and development support.
Allocate work based on project priorities, capacity, skills, and development opportunities, while monitoring workload and delivery performance.
Foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and disciplined execution.
Coordinate priorities and shared standards with Data Analytics teams across North America and Asia.
Maintain team knowledge management, including data access, technical patterns, and solution documentation.

Required Qualifications

University degree in computer science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, or another quantitative/technical discipline; Master’s degree preferred.
10+ years of relevant business and technology experience, including significant experience in data analytics, automation, AI, or software solution delivery. A combination of audit and advanced analytics/automation experience is preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading complex analytics, automation, or AI initiatives from concept through secure, reliable production, including solution design, effort estimation, resource planning, milestone management, execution oversight, risk management, and implementation.

jobs.title: Director, Public & Alternative Investments, Data Platforms
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

The Role

As Director, Data Engineering for the Public Markets and Alternate Assets (PMAA) team, you will build and publish the enterprise market data products that power investment strategies across our public markets and alternate assets businesses. Partnering closely with your business-aligned product owner, you will lead a talented team of data engineers and analysts and own the end-to-end lifecycle of PMAA data, from vendor and internal feeds through to trusted, well-documented data products used by investment teams, analytics platforms and AI agents. You will set the technical direction for a modern AWS data platform, establish the semantic and knowledge graph foundations that connect data across asset classes, and ensure every data product meets the standards of timeliness, quality, licensing compliance and control that investment decisions demand.

The Team

CPP Investments invests across public and private markets, supported by technology and data capabilities that enable informed investment decisions and long-term value creation.

Within PMAA, this role leads market data engineering and the development of enterprise data products that support investment professionals, quantitative and research teams. The team works with investment, product, architecture, technology and governance partners to deliver reliable, accessible and AI-ready market data.

Accountabilities

Define and execute the multi-year data engineering strategy and roadmap for PMAA market data products, partnering with the product owner to align priorities with investment needs and enterprise architecture standards.
Own the target-state AWS data platform architecture across ingestion, storage, processing, orchestration, governance and consumption, making design and build-versus-buy decisions that balance scalability, resilience, security and cost.
Lead the development and adoption of enterprise data products across public and private markets, including pricing, reference data, corporate actions and benchmarks, with clear ownership, data contracts, service levels and documentation.
Establish semantic data capabilities, including RDF knowledge graphs on Amazon Neptune, and enable governed access to AI-ready data through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, agent skills and Amazon Quick.
Ensure reliable, timely and secure data delivery through observability, automated quality controls, incident management, AWS Lake Formation, data lineage and market data licensing and entitlement controls.
Lead agile roadmap delivery and engineering excellence, embedding CI/CD, infrastructure as code, automated testing and reusable frameworks while engaging senior stakeholders, investment teams and strategic technology and data partners.
Build, coach and develop an inclusive, high-performing engineering team, fostering accountability, collaboration, continuous learning and career growth.

What You Bring

Undergraduate degree or college diploma in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field; a graduate degree is an asset.
10+ years of progressive experience in data engineering, data platforms or software engineering, including 5+ years leading engineering teams, with demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale, cloud-native data platforms and leading complex agile programs.
Strong understanding of capital markets, investment management and market and reference data, including experience with major data vendors, licensing, entitlements and usage controls; private markets experience is an asset.
Advanced AWS architecture expertise equivalent to Solutions Architect – Professional, including security, IAM, networking, resilience and cost optimization, together with hands-on technical depth in Apache Spark (PySpark or Scala), AWS Glue or EMR, Airflow/MWAA, AWS DMS and Amazon RDS/Aurora.
Expertise in enterprise data product design, AWS Lake Formation governance, data contracts, service levels and consumption patterns, along with RDF, SPARQL, ontology design, Amazon Neptune, MCP servers, agent skills and AI-assisted analytics using Amazon Quick.
Ability to guide engineering teams across cloud-native development, data quality, observability and delivery practices. Experience with lakehouse technologies, Python, SQL, CI/CD, infrastructure as code, data cataloguing, financial ontologies, Amazon Bedrock or GraphRAG is an asset; relevant AWS certifications are also assets.
Inclusive people leadership, sound judgment and strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to investment professionals and executives, influence stakeholders and manage strategic vendor partnerships.

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

This takes hard work and innovation, and we need more like-minded people on our team.

Lead security services that protect our business, strengthen client trust, and enable growth.

THE OPPORTUNITY

At Element Fleet Management, we're looking for a Director of Services to lead our Information Security Services organization. Reporting to the Chief Information Security Officer, you'll oversee five critical service lines, ensuring security expertise is embedded early in business decisions, projects, and client engagements.

You'll shape a scalable security services model, lead a multidisciplinary team, and deliver consistent, high-quality services that reduce risk while supporting business priorities and client commitments.

What You Will Own

Third-Party Risk: Lead the third-party risk program, including policies, vendor assessments, risk ratings, risk acceptance, and security reviews of vendor and client contracts.
Security Architecture and Engineering: Oversee security reviews of applications, cloud environments, integrations, and data flows. Establish secure design standards and reference architectures.
Security Advisory and Risk: Provide security guidance from project initiation, manage the risk register and exception process, and lead escalations involving high-risk matters.
Client Security Response: Oversee responses to client security questionnaires, due diligence requests, and audit inquiries, partnering with Sales, Legal, and Compliance.
Security Services Operations: Establish centralized intake, prioritization, service-level tracking, and performance metrics. Own the services roadmap, budget, resources, and supporting technology.
Governance and Assurance: Maintain alignment with ISO 27001, SOC 2, and NIST frameworks, supporting audit readiness and continuous improvement.

You Should Consider This Role If

You bring 10+ years of experience in information security, risk management, or governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), including at least 4 years leading teams.
You've successfully led a security services or advisory function spanning multiple disciplines.
You have strong knowledge of security architecture, cloud security, and industry security frameworks.
You have experience managing third-party risk programs and reviewing contractual security requirements.
You're comfortable managing external partners and contractors, balancing service quality, scope, and cost.
You combine strategic thinking with sound risk-based judgment and operational discipline.

Additional assets include a relevant degree, certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CISA, CCSP, or CTPRP, experience with GRC platforms and automation, or a background in a regulated or client-facing security environment.

Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team across five security service lines.
Establish clear accountabilities, service expectations, and performance measures.
Foster collaboration across Technology, Legal, Procurement, Sales, and Compliance.
Lead external advisors and assessment partners to deliver consistent, high-quality outcomes.
Champion proactive security engagement, continuous improvement, and scalable service delivery.

YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO TELL US

How you've built or improved a security services function to deliver measurable business value.
How you've balanced competing security priorities while maintaining service quality and managing risk.
How you've influenced senior stakeholders to incorporate security earlier in business decisions.
How you've developed teams, strengthened partnerships, and improved operational effectiveness.

At Element Fleet Management, security plays a critical role in enabling our business and maintaining client confidence.

This is an opportunity to shape how security services are delivered across the organization, influence strategic decisions, and build a service model that supports innovation, responsible risk management, and long-term growth.

You'll work alongside business and technology leaders, lead a talented team, and make a meaningful impact on how we protect our business and serve our clients.

Job Description

Posting Date: November 26, 2026

Closing Date: January 4, 2027

The Faculty of Education at the University of Alberta invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor in Artificial Intelligence in Education, with a focus on the ethical, equitable, and contextually responsive development, use, and critical examination of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in educational contexts.

We seek an outstanding emerging scholar whose research advances understanding of how artificial intelligence and related digital technologies are shaping and transforming education, including their implications for teaching, learning, curriculum, assessment, educational equity, and professional practice. The successful candidate will establish an innovative and independent research program that critically engages with the opportunities, challenges, and broader social implications of technological change in education.

This Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position is associated with Dr. Ig Bittencourt's Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair of Canada in Artificial Intelligence for Learning Equity at the University of Alberta. The appointment offers opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration while supporting the development of a distinctive and independent program of research grounded in educational scholarship and responsive to the needs and aspirations of diverse learners, educators, and communities.

The successful candidate will hold an academic appointment in the Faculty of Education.

Priority Areas of Research

Applications are invited from emerging scholars whose research advances the ethical, equitable, and contextually responsive understanding, development, use, and critical examination of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in education.

Areas of research interest may include, but are not limited to:

AI, digital technologies, and teaching and learning: The implications of artificial intelligence, generative AI, and emerging digital technologies for pedagogy, curriculum, assessment, learning environments, educational experiences, and teacher professional judgment.
Educational equity, ethics, and social justice: Research examining algorithmic bias, accessibility, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and the potential of AI and digital technologies to both reduce and reproduce educational and social inequities.
Critical and sociocultural perspectives on technology: Critical examinations of the relationships among technological change, educational policy, institutional practices, power, human agency, and the social, cultural, and political purposes of education.
Design, development, and evaluation of educational technologies: Research involving AI-enabled learning environments, adaptive learning systems, learning analytics, multimodal technologies, assistive technologies, and other innovative digital approaches to teaching and learning.
Indigenous education, knowledge systems, and digital sovereignty: Research that attends to Indigenous educational sovereignty, Indigenous data sovereignty, relational accountability, and the implications of AI and digital technologies for Indigenous languages, knowledges, teaching, and learning, developed through respectful and reciprocal relationships where appropriate.
Digital literacy, professional learning, and educational leadership: Research examining how educators, learners, and educational institutions develop the knowledge, critical capacities, professional practices, and governance approaches needed to engage responsibly with AI and emerging digital technologies.
Technology across diverse educational contexts: Research investigating AI and digital technologies in K–12, postsecondary, adult, professional, informal, community-based, rural, remote, and resource-constrained educational settings.

The successful candidate will develop an independent, externally funded research program and contribute to interdisciplinary collaborations across the University of Alberta, including opportunities to collaborate with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair of Canada in Artificial Intelligence for Learning Equity.

Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders Program Eligibility and Appointment

Applicants Must Be

Internationally based (working and residing outside of Canada as of October 14th, 2026).
An early career researcher, defined as being within five (5) years of the start date of their first research-related appointment (minus eligible leaves of absence, such as parental, medical, community, or bereavement leave) as of the posting date.
Be able to begin full-time employment at the University of Alberta no later than October 14th, 2027.

Successful nominees will be appointed at the University of Alberta as:

Assistant tenure-track Professor.
Successful nominees will be expected to start their position no later than October 14th, 2027.
The award value is $100,000 per year over six years and is renewable for up to six additional years at the same amount.
Chairholders will be required to take up their appointment on a full-time basis.

The University of Alberta recognizes the legitimate impact that life circumstances (e.g., maternity leave, parental leave, leaves due to illness, leaves due to caring for family members, slowdowns due to chronic illness or disability, COVID-19 impacts, etc.) can have on a candidate’s record of research achievement and that these circumstances will be taken into careful consideration during the assessment process. Please consult the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada and Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders
for full program information, including further details on eligibility criteria and application requirements.

The Role And Responsibilities

The Assistant Professor role is a starting point on the academic faculty member career pathway at the University of Alberta. Faculty members are full members of the Faculty and play an active role in democratic processes and governance. The responsibilities of the role include active participation in teaching, research, and service:

Teaching: The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching, curriculum development, and student supervision and mentorship within the Faculty of Education. Teaching responsibilities may include artificial intelligence in education, digital technologies and learning, educational technology, critical digital literacy, technology-enhanced pedagogy, research methodologies, and related areas aligned with the candidate's expertise and Faculty priorities.
The successful candidate will be expected to support inclusive, engaging, and critically informed learning environments, contributing to the preparation of educators, researchers, and educational leaders who can thoughtfully and ethically engage with artificial intelligence and emerging digital technologies in their professional practice.
Research: The successful candidate will be expected to initiate and advance an innovative, independent, and externally funded research program. The successful candidate will conduct and disseminate high-quality research, develop interdisciplinary collaborations, and translate findings into applications relevant to artificial intelligence, education, and equity. The position encourages collaboration with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair and the broader interdisciplinary research community at the U of A.
Service: The successful candidate will be expected to participate in service and professional development activities of the program area, Faculty, and University through collegial service, academic governance, mentorship, and collaborative initiatives. The successful candidate is also encouraged to engage with external partners and stakeholders in the technology and education sectors, including local, provincial, national, and international organizations, school divisions, and Indigenous communities and organizations, to support knowledge mobilization and the application of knowledge to the public.

Role and Expectations

The Successful Candidate Will Be Expected To

Establish an innovative, independent, and externally funded research program focused on artificial intelligence in education, with meaningful engagement in the broader field of digital technologies.
Advance research that critically examines the educational, ethical, cultural, and social implications of AI and technological change.
Produce and mobilize high-quality scholarship that informs educational policy, professional practice, technological innovation, and public understanding.
Contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching, curriculum development, and the supervision and mentorship of students and research personnel.
Develop interdisciplinary research collaborations, including opportunities to work with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair and scholars across the University.
Engage collaboratively and reciprocally with educational professionals, communities, Indigenous organizations, policymakers, and other relevant partners, as appropriate to the research.
Contribute to collegial governance, service, and the intellectual life of the Faculty and University.

About the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders Program

Launched in December 2025, the Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time national initiative designed to support Canadian institutions in growing and sustaining a critical mass of expertise in priority areas identified by the Government of Canada to address pressing domestic and global challenges. While distinct from the senior research chairs, the successful early career researcher (ECR) nominee will be expected to establish an independent program of research that leverages potential synergies and collaborations with incoming institutional Canada Impact+ Research Chairs (CIRC) to accelerate the translation of discoveries into tangible social, environmental, and economic solutions.

About the Faculty of Education and the University of Alberta

The Faculty of Education is consistently ranked among the top faculties of education in Canada and globally. It is home to award-winning educators, internationally recognized researchers, and socially engaged scholars. Guided by All Together , the Faculty of Education's adaptive and integrated strategic plan, our research, teaching, and community engagement are grounded in commitments to ethical relationality, educational equity, Indigenous educational sovereignty, and the public good. We recognize that artificial intelligence and digital technologies are reshaping educational possibilities, relationships, and responsibilities. We seek scholars who will contribute to understanding and shaping these transformations in ways that advance inclusive excellence, educational opportunity, human flourishing, and the well-being of diverse communities.

The University of Alberta exists to inspire and ignite the human spirit in pursuit of a better tomorrow. Its work is rooted in a commitment to creating a university community where everyone feels valued, barriers to success are removed, and thriving connections are fostered while honouring Indigenous identities, languages, cultures and world views. As one of the world’s top 100 teaching and research universities, the U of A ranks among the Top 4 in Canada, providing a $19.4 billion annual economic impact in Alberta alone. CoCounsel Legal is Thomson Reuters' AI assistant for legal professionals. This role leads the part of it that makes it adaptable: the agent's ability to take on a customer's skills, connect to third-party systems, and remember what matters to each legal team.

We want an AI-native engineering leader who works at the forefront of AI-assisted development. You already build with coding agents and agent workflows, and you set the standard for how your teams do the same. You stay hands-on, make sound technical trade-offs, and plan strategically while the product and customer needs are still taking shape.

Location & Flexibility

This role will operate remotely in the United States
or Canada
OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.

This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery
: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.

Responsibilities

Strategic Account Governance & Growth

Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).
Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.
Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.
Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.
Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.
Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.
Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.
Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.
Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

Leadership & Talent Development

Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.
Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.
Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

Operational & Financial Stewardship

Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.
Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.
Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.
Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

Qualifications

10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.
Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.
Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.
Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.
Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.
Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.
Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.
Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.
Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.
Ability to translate complex delivery data into compelling narratives for QBRs and executive stakeholders.
Understanding of regulatory requirements in contact center operations (e.g., PCI, HIPAA, TCPA, PIPEDA) is a plus.

The Faculty of Education at the University of Alberta invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor in Artificial Intelligence in Education, with a focus on the ethical, equitable, and contextually responsive development, use, and critical examination of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in educational contexts.

We seek an outstanding emerging scholar whose research advances understanding of how artificial intelligence and related digital technologies are shaping and transforming education, including their implications for teaching, learning, curriculum, assessment, educational equity, and professional practice. The successful candidate will establish an innovative and independent research program that critically engages with the opportunities, challenges, and broader social implications of technological change in education.

This Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position is associated with Dr. Ig Bittencourt's Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair of Canada in Artificial Intelligence for Learning Equity at the University of Alberta. The appointment offers opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration while supporting the development of a distinctive and independent program of research grounded in educational scholarship and responsive to the needs and aspirations of diverse learners, educators, and communities.

The successful candidate will hold an academic appointment in the Faculty of Education.

Priority Areas of Research

Applications are invited from emerging scholars whose research advances the ethical, equitable, and contextually responsive understanding, development, use, and critical examination of artificial intelligence and digital technologies in education.

Areas of research interest may include, but are not limited to:

AI, digital technologies, and teaching and learning: The implications of artificial intelligence, generative AI, and emerging digital technologies for pedagogy, curriculum, assessment, learning environments, educational experiences, and teacher professional judgment.
Educational equity, ethics, and social justice: Research examining algorithmic bias, accessibility, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and the potential of AI and digital technologies to both reduce and reproduce educational and social inequities.
Critical and sociocultural perspectives on technology: Critical examinations of the relationships among technological change, educational policy, institutional practices, power, human agency, and the social, cultural, and political purposes of education.
Design, development, and evaluation of educational technologies: Research involving AI-enabled learning environments, adaptive learning systems, learning analytics, multimodal technologies, assistive technologies, and other innovative digital approaches to teaching and learning.
Indigenous education, knowledge systems, and digital sovereignty: Research that attends to Indigenous educational sovereignty, Indigenous data sovereignty, relational accountability, and the implications of AI and digital technologies for Indigenous languages, knowledges, teaching, and learning, developed through respectful and reciprocal relationships where appropriate.
Digital literacy, professional learning, and educational leadership: Research examining how educators, learners, and educational institutions develop the knowledge, critical capacities, professional practices, and governance approaches needed to engage responsibly with AI and emerging digital technologies.
Technology across diverse educational contexts: Research investigating AI and digital technologies in K–12, postsecondary, adult, professional, informal, community-based, rural, remote, and resource-constrained educational settings.

The successful candidate will develop an independent, externally funded research program and contribute to interdisciplinary collaborations across the University of Alberta, including opportunities to collaborate with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair of Canada in Artificial Intelligence for Learning Equity.

Internationally based (working and residing outside of Canada as of October 14th, 2026).

Successful nominees will be appointed at the University of Alberta as:

Assistant tenure-track Professor.
Successful nominees will be expected to start their position no later than October 14th, 2027.
The award value is $100,000 per year over six years and is renewable for up to six additional years at the same amount.
Chairholders will be required to take up their appointment on a full-time basis.

Please consult the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chairs of Canada and Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders
for full program information, including further details on eligibility criteria and application requirements.

The Role And Responsibilities

The Assistant Professor role is a starting point on the academic faculty member career pathway at the University of Alberta. Faculty members are full members of the Faculty and play an active role in democratic processes and governance. The responsibilities of the role include active participation in teaching, research, and service:

Teaching: The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and graduate teaching, curriculum development, and student supervision and mentorship within the Faculty of Education. Teaching responsibilities may include artificial intelligence in education, digital technologies and learning, educational technology, critical digital literacy, technology-enhanced pedagogy, research methodologies, and related areas aligned with the candidate's expertise and Faculty priorities.
The successful candidate will be expected to support inclusive, engaging, and critically informed learning environments, contributing to the preparation of educators, researchers, and educational leaders who can thoughtfully and ethically engage with artificial intelligence and emerging digital technologies in their professional practice.
Research: The successful candidate will be expected to initiate and advance an innovative, independent, and externally funded research program. The successful candidate will conduct and disseminate high-quality research, develop interdisciplinary collaborations, and translate findings into applications relevant to artificial intelligence, education, and equity. The position encourages collaboration with the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair and the broader interdisciplinary research community at the U of A.
Service: The successful candidate will be expected to participate in service and professional development activities of the program area, Faculty, and University through collegial service, academic governance, mentorship, and collaborative initiatives. The successful candidate is also encouraged to engage with external partners and stakeholders in the technology and education sectors, including local, provincial, national, and international organizations, school divisions, and Indigenous communities and organizations, to support knowledge mobilization and the application of knowledge to the public.

Role and Expectations

The Successful Candidate Will Be Expected To

Establish an innovative, independent, and externally funded research program focused on artificial intelligence in education, with meaningful engagement in the broader field of digital technologies.
Advance research that critically examines the educational, ethical, cultural, and social implications of AI and technological change.

Launched in December 2025, the Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time national initiative designed to support Canadian institutions in growing and sustaining a critical mass of expertise in priority areas identified by the Government of Canada to address pressing domestic and global challenges. About Leo Berwick

Who we are:

Leo Berwick is an innovative mergers and acquisitions consulting firm. We are comprised of top tier, experienced advisors from global law and accounting firms that add value to transactions as trusted partners throughout the deal life cycle. At Leo Berwick, we hire the best and the brightest. Our teams deliver a dedicated and customized service to every client.

As a growth-stage company, we move quickly, work collaboratively, and value people who take initiative and thrive in a fast-paced environment. Our culture is grounded in high performance, continuous learning, and the shared ambition to build something exceptional, together.

What We’re Looking For

Leo Berwick is looking for a Head of Engineering to join our technology team, reporting to the Chief Technology Officer. This role is based in the Greater Toronto Area, Ontario, with a hybrid work arrangement of 2 days per week in office.

We’re looking for a deeply technical engineering leader who has built and scaled products in fast-moving SaaS environments and personally led the architecture and delivery of production agentic AI solutions. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between architecture, engineering delivery, and team leadership, and who has the technical credibility to coach and develop experienced Staff and senior engineers.

The Head of Engineering will own end-to-end software development and lead the architecture, delivery, and scaling of our technology platforms. Working closely with senior leadership, engineers, and internal subject matter experts, this individual will lead a small, experienced engineering team across onshore and offshore locations. With an established platform foundation, direct access to internal users, and subject matter expertise already available, the team can build and test products immediately. As the business evolves, the role may expand into leadership of distinct SaaS product areas, with scope to grow into leadership of distinct SaaS product areas.

You’re the right fit for this role if you –

Take ownership, make sound decisions, and turn ambitious product goals into delivered solutions.
Thrive in a fast-moving, evolving environment while maintaining strong engineering discipline.
Communicate openly and clearly with technical teams, business leaders, and other stakeholders.
Invest in coaching others and building a collaborative, accountable, high-performing team.

What You'll Do

Engineering strategy and architecture

Own end-to-end engineering execution across the platform, from technical planning through development, release, and continuous improvement.
Lead architecture decisions and governance across scalable, reliable systems, including oversight of data engineering capabilities.
Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to translate complex needs into achievable product and technical roadmaps.

Product delivery and engineering processes

Build, implement, and continuously improve software development life cycle (SDLC) practices, delivery processes, and engineering quality standards.
Set engineering priorities and deliver products that support internal business needs and future SaaS opportunities.
Lead the architecture and delivery of agentic AI products, applying established agentic engineering expertise to build production-ready solutions.

Team leadership and stakeholder partnership

Lead an initial team of approximately seven to eight predominantly senior engineers across onshore and offshore locations.
Coach senior and staff engineers, strengthen technical ownership, and cultivate a culture of accountability and continuous learning.
Communicate progress, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations effectively to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

What You Bring

10+ years of software engineering experience, including substantial technical leadership and engineering management experience.
Deep architectural expertise in agentic systems and proven experience designing, building, and delivering agentic AI products with production agentic systems you can point to and discuss in depth.
Several years of experience in a fast-paced SaaS or product-building environment.
Proven ability to establish and implement software development life cycle (SDLC) processes, engineering standards, and architectural governance from the ground up.
Demonstrated success building and mentoring high-performing teams of senior and staff engineers.
Strong stakeholder communication skills and a record of delivering effectively through changing business and technology environments.
Ability and interest to learn M&A and private capital transaction workflows and translate domain expertise into practical technology solutions.
A strong technical academic background is preferred, but demonstrated engineering delivery and leadership experience take precedence over a particular degree or designation.

What Success Looks Like In Year One

Own and advance a clear architectural and engineering delivery roadmap for the existing platform and priority products.
Establish consistent SDLC practices, architectural governance, and reliable engineering delivery across the team.
Develop a high-performing senior engineering team that delivers meaningful improvements to internal users and supports future product expansion.
Deliver at least one agentic AI product into production use by internal teams.

Unlimited paid time off including 2 weeks of disconnected time each year
Flexible working arrangements – remote and location flexibility
Tuition reimbursement
Attractive medical, dental insurance
Pension & retirement contributions
Monthly fringe benefit stipend (up to $400)
Additional benefits to support your physical and mental wellness

This is a permanent full-time role with a base salary range of $250,000 - $300,000 CAD. Placement within the range will depend on relevant experience and scope of responsibility.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.
